scope: C11AtomicOperation distinguishes seventeen Clang spellings from GNU AtomicOperation. The Clang target profiles preserve object access, ordinary expected-buffer writes, initialization, weak/strong CAS, orders, argument conversions, and evaluated lock-free-query operands. Linux targets remain GNU profiles and diagnose __c11_atomic calls rather than mixing GNU layout with Clang semantics.

Cross-compiler tests check source typing on x86_64/aarch64 Darwin and x86_64 Microsoft targets using Clang. Pointer/sign/qualifier warnings are promoted to errors in the strict constraint matrix; exploratory diagnostics retain plain Clang acceptance. Invalid memory orders and unsupported function-pointer arithmetic have explicit Toucan diagnostics.

The unchanged Clang resource stdatomic header is parsed with its resource include path and explicit freestanding configuration on all three Clang targets. The unchanged GNU header declarations pass both GNU targets with the target-specific predefined macros. GNU operational macros require the separate __auto_type implementation; the exact current diagnostic is preserved.

Earlier atomic-type evidence incorrectly named least8 as the first missing header predefine. Rechecking GCC13 stdatomic.h identifies __CHAR16_TYPE__ at line55, followed by __CHAR32_TYPE__. This layer adds both and corrects GNU fast16/32 to long, verified against native GCC 13 and cross-GCC 13 dumps. Required scalar lock-free macros are 2 for these default profiles, without a 16-byte guarantee.

The positive C program executes under native Clang 18 at O0 and O2 on x86_64 Linux. They establish compiler runtime behavior independently of the Toucan semantic analysis. Toucan does not generate their machine code or implement a concurrent memory model. These native executions do not establish native Darwin/Windows ABI compatibility.

Two separate native compiler failures are retained at O0 and O2: failed compare-exchange on an expanded three-byte record does not copy the value back to its ordinary expected buffer, and fetch-add on a pointer-to-VLA uses a zero stride. Their complete source, LLVM, commands, binary hashes and returncodes remain in this report. Retained C11 semantics are not weakened to model these compiler codegen failures.

Positive native cases cover scalar/record initialization, ordered load/store/exchange, scalar and four-byte-record compare-exchange, integer/floating/Boolean fetch operations, fixed-size pointer scaling, VLA initialization/load, fences and query operand evaluation. Three-byte-record compare-exchange and VLA fetch-add are excluded from positive claims; their failing compiler probes are explicit.

Six checked seed/profile cases walk the retained graph, while focused source tests compare ordinary and retained units and preserve a single local VLA bound through load/fetch-add/exchange result types. All operations suppress a surrounding Clang constant query when their operands/effects are observable.

The 24-level query chain completes on the immutable release binary with the bounded atomic-query cache. Four ordinary semantic allocation samples exactly match c462cce. This is not a frontend speed benchmark or a new sanitizer campaign.

Selected atomic Rust storage/call ABI remains an explicit diagnostic in the earlier atomic-type layer. C Bool macro constants preserve rank 0, 8-bit, unsigned semantic metadata but currently project to Rust u8 via the existing width/sign macro emitter; Bool projection is a separate binding follow-up.
